passages.locator: St Xavier’s College, Calcutta, and at Christ’s College, Cambridge
passages.excerpt_preview: He studied at St Xavier’s College, Calcutta, and at Christ’s College, Cambridge, and returned to India in 1885 to join Presidency College as officiating professor of physics.
The Institute was conceived as a place for research across disciplines and for sharing knowledge.
In 1917 he founded the Bose Research Institute, later Bose Institute, and served as its first director.
Bose was initially appointed on lower pay than European colleagues, protested while continuing to teach, and received equal pay retrospectively after three years.
agadish Chandra Bose was born on 30 November 1858 at Mymensingh.
At Presidency College he developed a laboratory and began research on electromagnetic waves in the 1890s.
